title: Parameter sniffing and plan instability
description: Understand parameter sniffing in SQL Server, why it causes plan instability, and practical mitigation strategies.

data.text: Parameter sniffing occurs when SQL Server compiles a stored procedure or parameterized query using the actual parameter values passed on the first execution. If those values are not representative of typical workloads, the resulting plan may be optimal for the first call but poor for subsequent calls with different parameter values.

When a stored procedure is executed, SQL Server compiles a plan and caches it. During compilation, the optimizer inspects the current parameter values and uses them to estimate row counts. The cached plan is then reused for later executions, even when new parameter values would produce a different optimal plan.

data.title: Stored procedure with sniffing risk
data.content: A procedure that filters by CustomerID may produce a seek plan for a single customer and a scan plan for a broad range. The first caller determines the plan for everyone.

data.title: Common signs
items: A query runs fast for some parameter values and slow for others
Performance improves after the plan cache is cleared or the procedure is recompiled
A plan with an index seek appears in the cache even when a scan would be better for typical values

data.title: Practical fixes
items: Use OPTION (RECOMPILE) to force a fresh compile for each execution
Use OPTIMIZE FOR to tell the optimizer to use a representative value
Use OPTIMIZE FOR UNKNOWN to ignore the sniffed value and use density-based estimates
Redesign the procedure into separate procedures for distinct parameter patterns
Use local variables to hide the actual parameter value from the optimizer

data.title: Use OPTION (RECOMPILE)
data.content: For high-volatility procedures, recompilation removes the stale plan problem at the cost of extra CPU.

data.title: Plan guides and forced plans
data.text: In some environments, you can use plan guides or query store forced plans to stabilize performance. These are advanced techniques and should be used with caution because they bypass normal optimization and can become outdated as data changes.

data.title: Takeaway
points: Parameter sniffing caches a plan based on first-execution values
It causes instability when parameter distributions vary widely
RECOMPILE, OPTIMIZE FOR, and redesign are common mitigations
Query Store forced plans are a last resort for production stabilization
data.takeaway: Parameter sniffing is a feature, not a bug, but it becomes a problem when data distributions are skewed. Design procedures with uniform workloads in mind, or use recompilation strategically.
